subject.title: [Feature]: Support multi-target cron delivery from configured target sets

question: Should cron expose a general explicit `delivery.targets` list, an operator-managed named target set, or both—and what should the durable partial-failure and webhook semantics be?
rationale: This decision defines a public stored-job/configuration contract and determines whether the feature belongs in cron delivery alone or also requires an operator target-set surface; prior unmerged implementations demonstrate that this cannot be safely inferred from a narrow patch.

options.title: Explicit target list first
options.body: Add a bounded `delivery.targets` announce contract with per-target resolution and audit records, while deferring named target sets until their configuration owner is designed.

options.title: Design target sets together
options.body: Approve both explicit targets and a named target-set owner only if maintainers want centrally managed routing as part of the initial public contract.

options.title: Keep delivery single-target
options.body: Decline core fan-out and direct users to separate schedules or an external plugin/workflow until a stronger product need is established.

recommendation.title: Explicit target list first
recommendation.body: Add a bounded `delivery.targets` announce contract with per-target resolution and audit records, while deferring named target sets until their configuration owner is designed.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the most directly affected destination-session and outbound delivery invariant.
